audit_findings.title: Tax-equity VIE cash flows may not belong to CMS common shareholders
audit_findings.mechanism: OE numerator through consolidated depreciation add-backs, capital expenditures, tax benefits, and cash flows that may be economically allocated to tax-equity investors rather than CMS common
audit_findings.evidence: Under the associated limited liability company agreement, the tax equity investor is guaranteed preferred returns from the entity.
audit_findings.explanation: A claim-basis mismatch is demonstrated if parent-attributable income is combined with 100 percent of consolidated VIE cash-flow components. Its direction is mixed because removing investor-funded capital expenditure would increase OE, while removing depreciation or other benefits belonging to tax-equity investors would decrease OE. The filed VIE asset base was $1,652 million, including $1,569 million of plant and construction work in progress, compared with the $841.3 million OE anchor, so the mismatch is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation even though the attributable amount cannot be determined from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild each historical and anchor OE component using the VIE-level HLBV allocation schedules, capital accounts, distributions, investor contributions, and project cash-flow statements; then rerun all scenarios on the CMS-common-attributable amounts.

audit_findings.title: Convertible-note dilution is inconsistent with an interest-burdened numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: computed 21.90 million full-conversion shares; removing them changes bear/base/bull value per share from $27.31/$33.93/$39.92 to approximately $29.21/$36.30/$42.70
audit_findings.mechanism: share denominator and, if conversion is assumed, the associated interest burden in OE
audit_findings.evidence: Upon conversion, the convertible senior notes are required to be paid in cash with only amounts exceeding the principal permitted to be settled in shares.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual inconsistency is demonstrated: $1.8 billion of notes have conversion equivalents of approximately 21.90 million shares, although principal must be settled in cash and only the premium may be share-settled. The current $68.46 share price is also below the filed conversion prices of $73.61 and $90.61. Even the conservative upper-bound correction of deleting all 21.90 million shares raises bull value only to about $42.70, still $25.76 below the market price, so it does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Replace the full-conversion equivalents with year-by-year net-share-settlement dilution based on projected stock prices and reconcile any assumed conversion date with interest savings and cash settlement of principal.

audit_findings.title: Parent preferred stock may be included in owner earnings but excluded from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $10 million annual preferred dividend and $224 million senior claim; computed base-case effect is approximately $133 million or $0.39 per share through OE, versus $0.67 per share if the $224 million claim is deducted in the bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: OE numerator before income available to common, or alternatively the equity bridge for the senior preferred claim
audit_findings.evidence: The Series C preferred stock ranks senior to CMS Energy’s common stock with respect to dividend rights and distribution rights upon liquidation.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing shows $1,071 million of net income attributable to CMS Energy, a $10 million preferred dividend, and $1,061 million available to common. If the OE calculation began before that dividend, the common numerator is overstated. However, the base-case capitalization of the $10 million annual amount is only about $0.39 per share; even the alternative $224 million bridge deduction is only $0.67 per share, compared with the $34.53 gap between base value and market price. The two treatments must not be applied together.
audit_findings.action: Trace the starting income line for every OE year. If it is pre-preferred, either deduct preferred dividends from OE consistently or deduct the $224 million senior claim in the bridge, and rerun without double counting.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor may retain a nonrecurring debt-extinguishment gain
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $72 million pre-tax gain; computed pre-tax upper-bound reduction is approximately $957 million or $2.84 per share in base and $1,130 million or $3.36 per share in bull
audit_findings.mechanism: 2025 anchor OE, which is capitalized throughout the explicit forecast and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: On a consolidated basis, CMS Energy’s repurchase of Consumers’ first mortgage bonds was accounted for as a debt extinguishment and resulted in a pre-tax gain of $ 72 million during 2025, which was recorded in other income on CMS Energy’s consolidated statements of income.
audit_findings.explanation: Retention of the gain is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated error, because the supplied OE reconciliation does not show whether it was purged. If the entire pre-tax gain remains, the computed upper-bound effect is meaningful but only reduces value: bull value would fall from $39.92 to about $36.56, remaining far below the $68.46 market price. Any tax adjustment would make the effect smaller, so it cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $72 million other-income gain and its actual tax effect through the 2025 OE workpaper; if retained, remove the after-tax amount from the anchor and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The static share ceiling may omit dilution required to finance projected growth
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $3.0 billion new equity-program capacity; 6.5 million shares issued for $495 million during the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: future share denominator and the allocation of growth-funded OE between current and newly issued shareholders
audit_findings.evidence: CMS Energy and Consumers rely on the capital markets to fund their robust capital plan.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking financing risk rather than an error presently established in the valuation. CMS has authorized a new $3.0 billion equity program after issuing 6.5 million shares in the first half of 2026, while the valuation projects growth using a static 336.670378 million-share ceiling. Future issuance could dilute current holders, but its amount, timing, price, and incremental OE contribution are not yet established.
audit_findings.action: At each financing update, forecast the debt/equity funding mix for the explicit-period capital plan, add expected net new common shares by year, attribute incremental OE to the financed investment, and rerun the per-share scenarios when issuance is contracted or reasonably estimable.

audit_findings.title: Material retirement obligations remain unmeasured
audit_findings.mechanism: future retirement and remediation cash outlays in OE, or a bridge liability to the extent costs are unrecoverable from customers
audit_findings.evidence: Consumers has been recording incremental AROs for legacy impoundments and CCR management units when a reasonable estimate of the fair value of the associated costs can be made, and the ultimate amount of any resulting ARO could be material.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing reports $808 million of recorded AROs at June 30, 2026, but the finding concerns additional CCR obligations that cannot yet be reasonably estimated. The company identified no legacy impoundments, but CCR-management-unit evaluation and regulatory outcomes remain incomplete. Incremental common-equity cost depends on the undiscounted outlays, timing, and regulatory recovery, so the record establishes exposure but cannot establish materiality or a valuation amount.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the completed CCR-management-unit inventory, engineering cost ranges, payment schedule, recorded-versus-unrecorded ARO reconciliation, and regulatory recovery evidence; model unrecovered or materially lagged cash costs in OE and rerun when estimable.
